label: Complete Manifolds and the Two Great Theorems
notes: This chapter, drawn from printed pages 144 through 154, asks when a Riemannian manifold has geodesics that extend forever. Completeness is the bridge between local geodesic theory and global geometry, and it powers the Hopf-Rinow and Cartan-Hadamard theorems that follow.

label: Geodesic Completeness
notes: A manifold is geodesically complete when every geodesic can be reparametrized to run over the entire real line. Equivalently the exponential map at each point is defined on the whole tangent space, so no geodesic ever falls off the edge of the manifold in finite time.

label: An Incomplete Manifold
notes: The punctured plane shows incompleteness concretely. A straight geodesic aimed at the missing origin reaches the puncture in finite arc length and cannot continue. The exponential map fails to be defined for the full tangent vector, so completeness genuinely constrains the geometry.

label: Metric Completeness
notes: Every connected Riemannian manifold becomes a metric space under the infimum of lengths of joining curves. Metric completeness asks that every Cauchy sequence converge. The deep content of Hopf-Rinow is that this analytic notion coincides exactly with the geometric notion of geodesic completeness.

label: The Hopf-Rinow Theorem
notes: Hopf-Rinow gathers four equivalent statements: the exponential map at one point is defined everywhere, closed bounded sets are compact, the manifold is metrically complete, and it is geodesically complete. Any single condition forces all the others on a connected manifold.

label: Minimizing Geodesics Exist
notes: A powerful corollary of Hopf-Rinow guarantees that any two points of a complete connected manifold are joined by a minimizing geodesic whose length equals their distance. Completeness thus upgrades the local existence of short geodesics into a global existence statement.

label: Proof Strategy of Hopf-Rinow
notes: The proof fixes a point and follows the unit geodesic toward the target, tracking the largest radius on which a minimizing geodesic reaches every sphere. A continuity and compactness argument shows this radius cannot stop short, so the geodesic arrives exactly at the target distance.

label: Conjugate Points and Curvature
notes: Conjugate points mark where nearby geodesics from a common origin refocus, signalling that the exponential map becomes singular. Jacobi fields measure this spreading, and nonpositive sectional curvature forces them to grow, so no refocusing and hence no conjugate points can occur.

label: The Cartan-Hadamard Theorem
notes: Cartan-Hadamard states that a complete simply connected manifold of nonpositive sectional curvature has its exponential map a diffeomorphism from the whole tangent space. Such a manifold is therefore diffeomorphic to Euclidean space and carries no conjugate points anywhere.

label: Exponential Map as Global Diffeomorphism
notes: Under the Cartan-Hadamard hypotheses the exponential map carries straight lines through the origin of the tangent space onto complete geodesics, with no folding or overlap. The flat tangent space becomes a faithful global chart for the curved manifold below it.

label: Consequences and Examples
notes: Hyperbolic space realizes Cartan-Hadamard with strictly negative curvature, exhibiting unique geodesics and exponential volume growth. The theorem rules out closed nonpositively curved simply connected manifolds and underlies comparison geometry, covering space arguments, and the study of nonpositively curved groups.

label: Recap: Completeness Organizes Global Geometry
notes: To summarize, geodesic and metric completeness coincide by Hopf-Rinow, which also yields minimizing geodesics between all points. Adding simple connectivity and nonpositive curvature gives Cartan-Hadamard, making the exponential map a diffeomorphism and fixing the global topology as Euclidean.
